web_title: 6. Multi-Year Financial Forensics, Capital Structure & ROIC
book_title: Chapter 6: The Forensic Ledger — Cash Flows, Convertibles, Leases & ROIC
question: Does DigitalOcean's 2019–2026 financial record show durable owner earnings and capital discipline once SBC, GPU leases, and convertible-note dilution are stripped bare?

epigraph.quote: Adjusted EBITDA flatters capital-intensive businesses by pretending that servers never wear out and stock grants never dilute.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: From FY2019 to Q3 2026, DigitalOcean scaled revenue more than 4x—from $270.5M to $901.4M in FY2025 and a $1.28B+ ARR run-rate [1][3][6]. GAAP operating income swung from $(21.3)M in FY2019 to $157.0M in FY2025 (17.4% margin) [3][6]. Yet cash-flow quality shifted in 2026 as GPU spending accelerated [2].

web_blocks.caption: DigitalOcean Historical Financial Forensics (FY2019–FY2025 & 9M/Q3 2026, $M)
web_blocks.takeaway: Operating leverage peaked in FY2025 (17.4% GAAP operating margin, $310.3M CFO), while 9M/Q3 2026 pairs 40% Q3 revenue growth with 50.1% gross margins and a sharp +82% YoY Q3 SBC rebound to $36.0M ($91.3M in 9M 2026). (*FY23 included a $31.3M MRSU reversal).

web_blocks.text: Forensic Deep Dive: SBC, Owner Earnings & GPU Lease Obligations

web_blocks.html: Two forensic adjustments expose the gap beneath headline Adjusted EBITDA ($144.2M in Q3 2026) [1]. First is Stock-Based Compensation. Contrary to FY2025's 8.9% downtrend ($80.3M), Q3 2026 SBC surged 82% YoY to $36.05M (~11.2% of sales; $91.28M in 9M 2026, +51.3% YoY) [2]. Cash payroll taxes for net-settled RSUs also drained $62.05M in 9M 2026 financing cash flows [2].

Second is Lease & Equipment Financing Explosion. Beyond $105.1M cash P&E, $19.3M software, and $75.1M equipment financing in 9M 2026, DigitalOcean added $750.0M in finance lease ROU assets and $492.9M in operating lease ROU assets [2]. Total finance lease and equipment financing liabilities jumped 7x to $923.6M PV ($1,059.2M undiscounted; $250.0M due in 2027), alongside $666.6M PV operating leases [2].

web_blocks.text: Convertible Senior Notes, Buybacks & Share-Count Architecture

web_blocks.html: Balance-sheet cleanup claims miss major remaining obligations [2][27]. While DigitalOcean retired $471.8M of 2030 Convertible Notes in July 2026 (triggering a $57.1M conversion charge), $312.3M of 2026 Convertible Notes still sit in current debt maturing December 1, 2026, alongside $153.2M of 2030 notes [2]. Off balance sheet, DOCN carries $2,955.2M in uncommenced 11.1-year colocation leases, a $785.0M MUFG Equipment Lease Facility (expandable to $1,025M), and a $128.1M software commitment [2][27]. On May 4, 2026, DOCN even amended its Credit Agreement so capitalized leases count at just 25% inside bank leverage covenants [2].

True invested capital has more than doubled [2]. Total assets hit $3,735.5M on September 30, 2026, with $2,051.8M in on-balance-sheet debt and lease liabilities ($461.6M debt + $666.6M operating leases + $923.6M finance leases/equipment financing) against $844.7M cash and marketable securities (~$1.21B net debt/leases; ~$2.62B net invested capital before $2.96B uncommenced leases) [2]. Lifting ROIC from ~1%–5% trailing (or 7%–9% FY25 normalized) above WACC requires disciplined utilization across this far heavier asset base [2][3].

web_blocks.title: The Forensic Bottom Line on Capital Quality
paragraphs: Core operating cash flow is solid ($318.1M in 9M 2026) and cash/liquidity ($844.7M + $396.9M revolver + $785M MUFG facility) covers the $312.3M Dec 2026 note maturity [2]. Yet $2.05B on-balance-sheet debt/leases, $2.96B uncommenced leases, +82% Q3 SBC growth, and a $1.0B ATM shelf confirm intense capital consumption [2][26].

web_blocks.html: Equity dilution accelerated sharply in 2026 despite an unused $100M buyback plan [2][26]. DOCN issued 11.95M shares in March 2026 ($887.9M net proceeds to repay its $500M Term Loan) and 12.54M shares in July 2026 ($1,473.9M net proceeds to retire $471.8M of deeply in-the-money 2030 notes) [2]. Basic shares jumped +28.2% YTD from 91.95M to 117.92M (118.00M as of October 29; 128M–129M Q4 diluted guide), before November 3's $1.0B ATM filing [1][2][26].

Insider and sponsor activity also merit scrutiny [28][29]. On November 19, 2026, CFO Matt Steinfort filed Form 144 to sell 75,000 shares (with no 10b5-1 plan date listed, after selling 10,000 shares on September 3), alongside regular 10b5-1 CEO and CAO sales [28]. Meanwhile, legacy sponsor Access Industries still holds 18.65M shares (15.86%) per Schedule 13D/A [29].

True economic invested capital now dwarfs prior estimates once finance leases ($923.6M), operating leases ($666.6M), and uncommenced colocation commitments ($2,955.2M) are included [2]. Until GPU utilization outpaces $250M annual lease amortization and +82% SBC growth, normalized ROIC remains compressed near cost of capital [2][3].

Cash flow durability remains the clearest dividing line between a top-line surge and a durable compounder [1][2]. Watching whether internal OCF can service $250M+ annual lease maturities and fund GPU refreshes without tapping the $1.0B ATM shelf is essential in 2027 [2][26].

book_paragraphs: Now we put on our forensic-accountant visors and examine DigitalOcean's Q3 2026 footnotes. Between FY2019 and FY2025, revenue tripled to $901.4 million and GAAP operating income swung to $157.0 million. Operating cash flow reached $318.1 million in 9M 2026. Yet the balance sheet underneath underwent a structural shift that headline EBITDA conceals.

First, stock-based compensation re-accelerated sharply. After dipping to $80.3 million (8.9% of sales) in FY2025, SBC jumped 82% year-over-year in Q3 2026 to $36.05 million—an annualized $144 million pace—and totaled $91.28 million in 9M 2026 (+51.3% YoY). Employee payroll taxes paid on net-settled equity awards simultaneously drained $62.05 million of cash.

Second, equity dilution expanded far faster than a single convertible cleanup. DigitalOcean sold 11.95 million shares in March 2026 ($887.9 million net) and 12.54 million shares in July 2026 ($1,473.9 million net). Shares outstanding jumped 28.2% in nine months from 91.95 million to 117.92 million. Q4 diluted share guidance now sits at 128 to 129 million, backed by a new $1.0 billion ATM equity shelf filed November 3, 2026.

Third, DigitalOcean replaced bond debt with a towering lease and equipment-financing wall. In 9M 2026, finance lease ROU additions hit $750.0 million and operating lease ROU additions hit $492.9 million. Total on-balance-sheet debt and lease liabilities reached $2,051.8 million ($1.21 billion net of cash and marketable securities). Off balance sheet sit $2,955.2 million of uncommenced 11.1-year colocation leases and a $785 million MUFG equipment lease facility.

Put simply, DigitalOcean is not near insolvency—its $844.7 million liquidity easily covers the remaining $312.3 million of 2026 notes maturing December 1, 2026. The real financial risk is capital efficiency and dilution: whether GPU cash flows can amortize $250 million in annual lease maturities without leaning on the $1.0 billion ATM program.

book_subsections.title: The Hidden Capex Line and the Convertible Cleanup
paragraphs: Hidden capital commitments sit inside Notes 8, 9, and 10 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q. Finance lease and equipment financing liabilities jumped sevenfold in nine months to $923.6 million present value ($1,059.2 million undiscounted). Scheduled payments reach $250.0 million in 2027, $249.1 million in 2028, and $245.2 million in 2029. Off balance sheet sit $2,955.2 million in uncommenced 11.1-year colocation leases, a $128.1 million software license deal, and the $785 million MUFG facility.

Notice the telltale covenant footprint in Note 7: on May 4, 2026, DigitalOcean amended its Credit Agreement so capitalized leases count at just 25% of their capitalized value inside bank 'Indebtedness' ratios. Meanwhile, $312.3 million of 2026 Convertible Notes still mature December 1, 2026, and CFO Matt Steinfort filed Form 144 on November 19, 2026 to sell 75,000 shares alongside Access Industries' 15.86% overhang.

book_subsections.title: The Convertible Cleanup and True Economic ROIC
paragraphs: Management did eliminate long-term convertible maturities by issuing 11.95 million shares in March 2026 to repay its $500 million Term Loan and 12.54 million shares in July 2026 to retire $471.8 million of deeply in-the-money 2030 notes (leaving $153.2 million outstanding). Yet pairing +28.2% nine-month share expansion with a November 3 $1.0 billion ATM equity shelf and an unused $100 million buyback plan turns equity into an active funding valve.

When we update invested capital to reflect Q3 2026's $3,735.5 million asset base—including $923.6 million in finance leases/equipment financing and $666.6 million in operating leases—net invested capital now approaches ~$2.62 billion before counting $2.96 billion of uncommenced colocation obligations. Against that capital base, normalized ROIC sits near or below cost of capital until new GPU clusters reach steady-state cash conversion.

book_subsections.title: Forensic Synthesis: Why Normalized ROIC Sits Near Cost of Capital
paragraphs: Stepping back across the seven-year financial arc from FY2019 ($270.5 million revenue, $(21.3) million operating loss) to FY2025 ($901.4 million revenue, $157.0 million operating income), DigitalOcean's operational progress is indisputable. Stock-based compensation was $80.3 million in FY2025 (8.9% of revenue), reasonable by software standards, and the July 2026 convertible note repurchase—retiring ~$472 million of 0.00% 2030 notes via a ~12.5 million share offering and leaving ~$153 million outstanding—eliminated near-term refinancing overhang.

Nevertheless, capital-allocation forensics force a sober conclusion. When we normalize FY2025 net income by removing the $52.6 million one-time tax benefit and measure after-tax operating profit against an invested capital base that includes leased data-center right-of-use assets and financed GPU equipment, DigitalOcean's economic ROIC sits in the 7% to 9% band. Until GPU utilization and Core Cloud pull-through lift ROIC decisively above 12%–15%, the business remains a cyclical, capital-intensive growth story rather than an asset-light compounder.

book_callouts.title: Owner Earnings Formula for DOCN
book_callouts.quote: True Owner Cash Flow = Operating Cash Flow − Cash Capex − Equipment Financing Additions − SBC.
book_callouts.text: Apply this formula every quarter in 2027, and add finance-lease ROU additions ($750M in 9M26) and RSU payroll taxes ($62.1M) to true capital charges. Watch whether OCF funds $250M annual lease maturities without tapping the $1.0B ATM shelf.
